summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 18.2 to Angular 19.2 with `ng update @angular/core@19 @angular/cli@19`, whose migration marked all seven NgModule-declared components `standalone: false` (standalone became the default in v19). The hop file listed no related packages, but @ngrx/* 18 pins `@angular/core@^18.0.0`, so @ngrx was bumped to 19.2.1. The one hand fix was `BrowserModule.withServerTransition({ appId })`, removed in v19: replaced with a plain `BrowserModule` import plus an explicit `APP_ID` provider keeping the same id. `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr` pass; `npm run test` still fails for the same pre-existing reason as at baseline.
changes: Angular packages 18.2.14 -> 19.2.25; @angular/cli and @angular-devkit/build-angular ^18.2.21 -> ^19.2.27. The CLI update also pulled typescript ~5.4.5 -> ~5.8.3 and zone.js ~0.14.10 -> ~0.15.1, both required by the Angular 19 peer ranges.

The core v19 migration added `standalone: false` to the @Component decorators of app, nav-menu, home, counter, fetch-data, fetch-employee and add-employee, since `standalone: true` is the default from v19 on and these components are declared by AppModule. Behaviour unchanged. The migration also reindented those decorators to 4 spaces; reindented by hand back to the original 2-space layout so the diff shows only the real change.

src/app/app.module.ts: Angular 19 removed `BrowserModule.withServerTransition()`, which failed to compile (TS2339) and invalidated the whole `imports` array (NG1010), cascading into ~15 bogus template errors about routerLink/ngClass/formGroup not being known properties. Replaced it with a plain `BrowserModule` import and added `{ provide: APP_ID, useValue: 'ng-cli-universal' }` to `providers`, which is the v19 way to set the app id that withServerTransition used to configure, so the SSR/client id stays 'ng-cli-universal'.

@ngrx/{store,effects,entity,router-store,store-devtools} ^18.1.1 -> ^19.2.1 via `ng update @ngrx/store@19`. Not listed in the hop file, but required: NgRx 18 declares a peer of @angular/core ^18.0.0. The NgRx schematic runner crashed after writing package.json (`Cannot find module '@angular-devkit/core'` from its own 6_0_0 migration, during the mid-run node_modules clean), so its migrations did not execute; checked the source afterwards and NgRx 19 needs no code change here (no deprecated APIs in use), and `npm install` + build confirm it.

Declined both optional migrations, per the smallest-correct-change rule: `use-application-builder` (keeps the existing `browser` builder and aspnet-prerendering SSR setup) and `provide-initializer` (no APP_INITIALIZER/ENVIRONMENT_INITIALIZER in src/).
package-lock.json regenerated by npm; verified with a from-scratch `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` (no --legacy-peer-deps or --force needed), followed by a clean build.
manual_followups: Tests still fail exactly as at baseline and for the same reason: the `test` target in angular.json lists the stylesheet as "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so Karma reports "Can't resolve 'styles.css'" and aborts before running any spec. Fixing that one path would let the suite run; left alone here because the hop rules only require that a baseline failure not get worse.

rxjs is still ^6.6.7. Angular 19 and NgRx 19 both still accept it (peer ^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0 / ^7.5.0), but rxjs 6 is end-of-life and the range will narrow; the rxjs 7 bump should happen in the next hop or two.

The app remains NgModule-based (now with explicit `standalone: false` on every component) on the deprecated `browser` builder with aspnet-prerendering SSR. Angular 20+ pushes harder on the application builder and standalone APIs, so this migration is still pending and will likely become mandatory in a later hop.

Deprecated/legacy devDeps remain unchanged (tslint, codelyzer, protractor, node-sass, core-js 2, @types/node 12, jasmine 3.10). None are exercised by the required checks, but they block a move to ESLint and will eventually conflict with newer Node/Angular.
